panels.title: Fan-Out: Destinations per Source
panels.description: Distinct destination IPs contacted by each source over the range. A host touching many peers is a scanner, a broken service, or P2P. Amber above 20, red above 50 — tune those thresholds to your network; on a small LAN everything stays green.

panels.title: Fan-Out over Time
panels.description: Distinct destinations per source in each 15-minute window, showing only sources that reach at least the Fan-out threshold. Without that threshold a large network emits thousands of series -- past Grafana's 1000-series cap, and unreadable anyway. A sudden vertical jump for one host is the scan signature worth chasing. The window is fixed at 15m rather than following the time picker, because windowing every source/destination pair at a finer grain does not finish on a busy network.

panels.title: Beacon Candidates
panels.description: Because active_timeout=5 caps duration_ms at ~5s, beacons cannot be found by flow duration — this ranks by repetition instead. Look for many 5-minute slots with flows/slot near 1 and a small mean size: that is something checking in on a timer. High flows/slot is an ordinary persistent connection (the VPN tunnel looks like that).

targets.query:
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

base = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: sum, timeSrc: "_start", createEmpty: false)

raw = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"])

union(tables: [
  base |> count() |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, dst_ip: r.dst_ip, k: "slots", v: r._value})),
  base |> sum()   |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, dst_ip: r.dst_ip, k: "bytes", v: r._value})),
  raw  |> count() |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, dst_ip: r.dst_ip, k: "records", v: r._value})),
])
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"], columnKey: ["k"], valueColumn: "v")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({pair: r.src_ip + " → " + r.dst_ip,
                      slots: r.slots, records: r.records, bytes: r.bytes,
                      per_slot: float(v: r.records) / float(v: r.slots),
                      mean_bytes: float(v: r.bytes) / float(v: r.records)}))
  |> sort(columns: ["slots"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 30)

panels.title: New Talker Pairs
panels.description: Source → destination pairs active in the selected range that never appeared in the preceding baseline window. Empty is the healthy answer on a stable network. Widen the time range or shorten the baseline to see more.

import "date"
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

seen = (start, stop) => from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: start, stop: stop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"])
  |> first()
  |> keep(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"])
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({pair: r.src_ip + " → " + r.dst_ip}))

recent = seen(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({pair: r.pair, era: 0}))

// era stays 0 only for keys that never appear in the baseline window
older = seen(start: date.sub(from: v.timeRangeStart, d: ${baseline}), stop: v.timeRangeStart)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({pair: r.pair, era: 1}))

union(tables: [recent, older])
  |> group(columns: ["pair"])
  |> sum(column: "era")
  |> group()
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.era == 0)
  |> keep(columns: ["pair"])
  |> sort(columns: ["pair"])

panels.title: New Destinations
panels.description: Destination IPs contacted in the selected range but absent from the baseline window, regardless of which host reached them. Newly contacted external addresses are the ones worth a second look.

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: cidr
list.label: CIDR filter
list.description: Restrict every panel to traffic with either endpoint in this range, e.g. 10.12.0.0/16, 10.12.6.0/24, or a bare IP. Leave empty for no filter. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round down to the enclosing octet boundary, so /20 behaves as /16 and may show a wider range than typed.

list.name: baseline
list.label: Baseline window
list.description: How far back to look for 'have we seen this before'. Measured backwards from the start of the dashboard time range.

list.name: fanout_min
list.label: Fan-out threshold
list.description: Minimum distinct destinations in a 15-minute window for a source to be plotted. Raise it on a busy network, lower it on a quiet one.
